systematic_issues.reason: The supplied target record omits actual control, exclusive-possession evidence, valuable consideration, and withheld occupancy agreements. Those authorities can still be useful background, but their distinctive predicates cannot be treated as target facts.

disagreements.reason: The resemblance of concepts is real, but the exact source identifies the provision as Andhra Pradesh law, while the controlling Delhi provision is independently supplied. That makes this unit unnecessary for the fixed Delhi issue rather than merely contextual.

The source is amalgamation-specific and expressly reserved, but it still directly discusses whether an assignment may attract Delhi rent-control proceedings. That supports limited background value, not direct application.
disagreements.source_quote: If there is any assignment in law, which may attract the provisions of the Delhi Rent Control Act, the landlord would be free to take recourse to the proceedings under that Act or in a regular civil action and such proceedings would be dealt with and decided by the appropriate authority in accordance with law.

disagreements.reason: The partnership-specific section 14(4) analysis has no target predicate, but the same supplied unit also reproduces the directly relevant section 14(1)(b) conduct and written-consent rule. Treating the entire unit as irrelevant would discard that source-supported component.
disagreements.source_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952 sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord

disagreements.reason: The retained-control proposition is useful, but the source is a later Goa-law synthesis and frames the proposition in a partnership setting. The target record supplies no partnership participation or actual-control facts, so omission of this unit would not leave the possession issue insufficiently covered.
disagreements.source_quote: If tenant is actively associated with the partnership business and retains the control over the tenancy premises with him, may be along with partners, the tenant may not be said to have parted with possession.

disagreements.reason: The source provides an analogical burden synthesis under Goa law, but its stated ingredients include exclusive possession and compensation or rent, which are not supplied in the target record. A direct Delhi burden rule is separately supplied, so this unit is supplemental rather than core.
disagreements.source_quote: Initial burden of proving subletting is on landlord but once he is able to establish that a third party is in exclusive possession of the premises and that tenant has no legal possession of the tenanted premises, the onus shifts to tenant to prove the nature of occupation of such third party and that he (tenant) continues to hold legal possession in tenancy premises.

disagreements.reason: The predecessor-statute burden passage is source-supported, but its distinctive inference depends on exclusive possession for valuable consideration and withholding the best written agreements. Those predicates are absent, and LAW:V09:KR_BURDEN already supplies the direct Delhi burden rule.
disagreements.source_quote: The respondent discharged the onus by leading evidence showing that the occupants were in exclusive possession of the apartments for valuable consideration.
